01 / Initial response

Case briefing

CASE FILE - 013–2025 TOP SECRET

The death of Eleanor Hayes

At 7:40 a.m. on 14 October, 2025, housekeeper June Bell discovered Eleanor Hayes, a 52-year-old investigative journalist, dead in Room 013 of the Bellwether Hotel. The room was locked from the inside. The only window was latched, and there were no signs of forced entry.

The medical examiner estimates the time of death between 10:00 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. the previous night. A heavy brass bookend was found near the desk. A half-finished cup of tea sat beside the victim's notebook.

VICTIMEleanor Hayes, 52
LOCATIONBellwether Hotel · Room 013
DATE FOUND14 October 2025 · 07:40
EST. TIME OF DEATH10:00–11:30 p.m.
CAUSEBlunt-force trauma
SCENELocked room · no forced entry
Eleanor had spent the week investigating falsified maintenance invoices at the hotel. Her final notebook page was torn out.
3 persons of interest7 evidence items1 unresolved question: the locked door

Your task: examine the evidence, test each suspect's story, connect the facts, and submit a reasoned conclusion. Findings are revealed through examination; there is no timer.

02 / Persons of interest

Suspect files

Interview each person. Look for gaps in their account.

♟
Hotel manager

Mara Voss

Managed the Bellwether for eleven years. Says she was in the lobby reviewing accounts until 10:45 p.m. Denies knowing what Eleanor was investigating.

⌁
Maintenance supervisor

Elias Ward

Controlled access to service corridors and master keys. Claims he left the hotel before 9:30 p.m. after finishing a repair on the fourth floor.

✒
Investigative colleague

Daniel Mercer

Worked with Eleanor on an earlier investigation. Admits arguing with her that evening, but says he left Room 013 at 9:15 p.m.

Room-service attendant · Witness

June Bell

Delivered a normal pot of tea to Room 013 at 9:52 p.m. Says she left the tray and did not return to the room that night.

04 / Chronology

Timeline of events

Separate verified timestamps from statements that still need corroboration.

20:55
Argument reported

Daniel Mercer admits arguing with Eleanor in Room 013. His claimed departure at 21:15 is not independently verified at this point.

WITNESS ACCOUNT
21:52
Tea delivered to Room 013

June Bell delivered a normally prepared pot of tea at 21:52. Later testing found sedative in Eleanor’s cup only—not in the tea remaining in the pot—indicating the dose was added after delivery.

DOCUMENTED
22:00–23:30
Estimated time of death

The medical examiner places the fatal assault within this window. The brass bookend is consistent with the blunt-force injury.

MEDICAL ESTIMATE
22:18
Service master key recorded

The register records Elias Ward’s master-key access at 22:18, after June delivered the tea. Pressure marks beneath a rewritten entry preserve “E. Ward”; the alteration was made after the key was returned.

ALTERED RECORD
22:41
Daniel appears at the café

The duplicate transaction record confirms Daniel bought coffee across the street. It supports his later whereabouts, but does not by itself prove where he was earlier.

RECEIPT CONFIRMED
07:40
Body discovered

Housekeeper June Bell finds Eleanor in Room 013. The door is locked, the window latched, and there are no obvious signs of forced entry.

DISCOVERY

Investigator’s caution: the register’s 22:18 entry is a documentary trace, not a direct eyewitness account. Weigh it alongside the physical evidence.
